title: Bioinformatician
what_they_do: Analyze large-scale biological datasets (genomes, transcriptomes, proteomes) using computational tools. Build pipelines, run statistical models, and visualize results to help biologists make discoveries.
day_in_life: Morning: check pipeline jobs on HPC cluster. Mid-day: meet wet-lab team to discuss RNA-seq experiment. Afternoon: write Snakemake pipeline for variant calling. Evening: generate publication figures in R.

title: Genetic Counselor
what_they_do: Interpret genetic test results and explain hereditary disease risks to patients and families. Help people understand genetic testing options, family planning, and medical management.
day_in_life: Morning: review prenatal genetic test results. Mid-day: counsel a couple about carrier screening options. Afternoon: attend multidisciplinary genetics case conference. Evening: update patient records and follow-up plans.

title: Biostatistician
what_they_do: Design experiments and clinical trials, apply statistical models to biological and medical data, and ensure that research conclusions are mathematically sound.
day_in_life: Morning: design sample size calculation for a new drug trial. Mid-day: run survival analysis on oncology data in R. Afternoon: present interim results to the clinical team. Evening: draft statistical methods section for a journal paper.

title: Clinical Genomics Scientist
what_they_do: Process patient DNA/RNA samples, run sequencing pipelines, identify disease-causing variants, and write clinical reports for physicians. Work in hospitals and diagnostic labs.
day_in_life: Morning: receive trio-exome samples from neonatal ICU. Mid-day: run variant calling pipeline on the clinical HPC. Afternoon: classify a novel BRCA1 variant using ACMG criteria. Evening: sign off report for the consulting oncologist.

title: Structural Biologist
what_they_do: Determine 3D structures of proteins, nucleic acids, and complexes using X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, or NMR. Use computational tools to model and interpret molecular architectures.
day_in_life: Morning: vitrify a new protein complex for cryo-EM data collection. Mid-day: process overnight data in RELION. Afternoon: fit atomic model into density map using Coot. Evening: run molecular dynamics simulation on the HPC.

title: Drug Discovery Scientist
what_they_do: Identify drug targets, design molecules, run virtual screening and docking studies, and collaborate with chemists and biologists to develop new therapeutics.
day_in_life: Morning: screen 100K compounds against a kinase target in silico. Mid-day: analyse ADMET hits and remove toxic candidates. Afternoon: discuss lead compounds with medicinal chemists. Evening: write docking protocol for the next target.

title: Microbiome Scientist
what_they_do: Study microbial communities in environments or human hosts using metagenomics, 16S rRNA analysis, and metabolomics. Link microbiome composition to health, agriculture, or environmental outcomes.
day_in_life: Morning: extract DNA from stool samples. Mid-day: run QIIME2 pipeline on 16S sequencing data. Afternoon: correlate gut bacteria with IBD patient outcomes. Evening: prepare seminar on probiotics research.

title: Evolutionary Biologist
what_they_do: Study how species evolve by analyzing DNA sequences, building phylogenetic trees, and modelling population genetics. Work in academia, museums, and conservation organizations.
day_in_life: Morning: collect plant leaf samples from the Western Ghats. Mid-day: extract DNA and run PCR for phylogenetic markers. Afternoon: build a maximum-likelihood tree in RAxML. Evening: draft a manuscript on cryptic species diversity.

title: Epigenomics Researcher
what_they_do: Study how chemical modifications to DNA and histones (methylation, acetylation) regulate gene expression without changing the sequence. Link epigenetic changes to disease, aging, and development.
day_in_life: Morning: process ChIP-seq data for histone marks in cancer cells. Mid-day: run differential methylation analysis with dmrseq in R. Afternoon: meet with oncology collaborators to discuss findings. Evening: annotate enhancer regions in the genome browser.

title: Agricultural Biotechnologist
what_they_do: Apply genomics and biotechnology to improve crop yield, disease resistance, and nutritional content. Develop GM crops, marker-assisted selection, and genome-edited plants.
day_in_life: Morning: genotype wheat varieties for rust resistance markers. Mid-day: review CRISPR-edited rice field trial data. Afternoon: analyze QTL mapping results for drought tolerance. Evening: write grant proposal for climate-resilient crops.

title: Biomedical Data Scientist
what_they_do: Apply machine learning and data science to electronic health records, imaging data, wearable sensor data, and clinical trial outcomes to improve healthcare decisions.
day_in_life: Morning: clean and preprocess 100K patient records from a hospital EHR. Mid-day: train a Random Forest model to predict sepsis onset. Afternoon: validate the model on a held-out cohort. Evening: present dashboard to hospital leadership.

title: Science Communicator / Educator
what_they_do: Translate complex biological research into accessible content for the public, students, or policymakers. Create educational materials, write science articles, produce videos, or teach.
india_colleges: Any BSc/MSc in Life Sciences + journalism/diploma
day_in_life: Morning: interview a researcher about their latest CRISPR paper. Mid-day: write a blog post explaining gene therapy to a lay audience. Afternoon: record a 3-minute explainer video for YouTube. Evening: moderate a Reddit AMA with a geneticist.
